news: New Chairman Shawn Pelsinger takes over July 24, 2026, succeeding Carl Albert (now Chairman Emeritus) - continued board stabilization.
Debt restructuring finalized: the $46.9M convertible note was swapped into a smaller $16.9M convertible plus a new $30M secured term note due 2028, easing near-term liquidity.

Business expansion continues - Wheels Up signed as BrokerOS launch customer (up to $12M subscription revenue), a deepened Palantir SurfOS partnership, and a new ALIA electric-aircraft demo in Hawai'i with BETA Technologies/Hawaiian Airlines - but the company remains deeply unprofitable.

Stock jumped ~8% today (to ~$27.85) helped by a positive Jim Cramer mention, though shares remain down nearly 50% since May on AI-capex/semiconductor-volatility concerns compounded by Nvidia's earlier exit from its equity stake.
FY2026 Q4/full-year earnings call set for July 27 at 5pm ET (7 days out) - focus will be data-center utilization, contract expansion, and capex/funding plans.
Analyst sentiment remains Strong Buy with a 12-month consensus target near $70-77, implying well over 100% upside from current levels despite the drawdown.
Continues diversifying beyond food delivery: NoScrubs laundry pilot now live in select LA neighborhoods, its first urban delivery partnership outside prepared food.
Board added Andreas Lieber (ex-Uber/Postmates/California Forever) as director effective June 22, 2026, replacing Sarfraz Maredia.
Stock still down ~47% YTD amid ongoing losses, but analyst consensus remains Buy (8 analysts, ~$17.58 target) - over 3x the current price.

FDA's Peptide Compounding Advisory Committee meets July 23-24 (3 days away) to review compounded GLP-1/peptide products - a binary regulatory catalyst for Hims' compounding-pharmacy revenue line; recommendations are non-binding but set the regulatory tone.
Sentiment is split heading in: Canaccord bullish at $40 vs. bears near $21, while the 13-analyst average target ($28-30) sits well below the current ~$33 price.

Business expansion continues - a $400M JPMorgan receivables facility and the $1.15B Eucalyptus acquisition (850K customers, ~$450M ARR across 8 international markets) support the GLP-1 growth story ahead of August 10 earnings.
Reports Q2 FY26 results after market close July 22 (2 days out); consensus calls for $3.92B revenue (+22% YoY) and $0.86 EPS, driven by Now Assist/AI Control Tower/Autonomous Workforce adoption.

Analyst views are mixed heading into the print: Evercore ($150), Bernstein ($236), and Oppenheimer ($130) all reiterate Outperform, but CLSA just initiated an Underperform citing rising costs and margin pressure.
Stock still down ~51% over the past year despite a recent bounce - a beat-and-raise quarter would be an important sentiment reset.

Shares fell another ~4% today (to ~$121) after news that Oracle's $16.5B AI data-center project in New Mexico has stalled on environmental-permitting hurdles, forcing a costly shift to on-site fuel cells.
S&P Global's July 9 downgrade to BBB- continues to weigh on sentiment, with free cash flow now reported at -$23.7B amid the AI capex buildout; OpenAI exposure was cited explicitly as a credit risk.
Stock is significantly underperforming the software sector (+1.5% the same day) and technicals (MACD, RSI) both signal further near-term weakness, even as some bulls see the selloff as overdone.
